title: SDK mini-standup: playbook, samples, and sticky blockers
content:
Date: 2026-11-30
Time: 10:15–10:45 PT (30m)
Facilitator: Maya Chen
Meeting type: compact weekly sync (micro-standup format)
Location: #devexp-mini-standup Slack, notes captured here

Attendees (present): Maya, Ethan, Sofia, Jonah, Priya (left early)
Attendees (async): Lila (notes later), Aaron

Quick agenda:
- 1) Playbook progress: lightweight quickstart templates + triage of feedback
- 2) Samples repo: restructure proposal + telemetry naming standards
- 3) SDK packaging and release cadence (monorepo vs package-per-sdk)
- 4) Blockers & decisions + action items

Round-robin updates (30s each):
- Maya: Playbook draft v0.3 ready. Focused on 3 short recipes: API key basic auth, streaming example, and embed+search pattern. Need final content for Rust example.
- Ethan: Samples refactor branch has static site generator prototype (MDX -> site). Found edge case: some quickstarts rely on local env vars (bad for web demos).
- Sofia: Telemetry event names inconsistent across samples (embedding.create vs embeddings.create). Working on mapping table. Also saw production issue where sample telemetry floods metrics on small PRs.
- Jonah: Packaging: migrating JS SDK to esbuild and rollup for smaller bundles. Also prototype for single-binary Python wheel using pex to simplify install in quickstarts.
- Priya: Docs: updating step-by-step CLI guide; needs acceptance criteria for quickstart coverage (3 cloud providers).

Notable discussion points / decisions:
- Quickstarts should guarantee "run-end-to-end within 10 minutes" in cloud notebook or local env. If more than 10 minutes, label as "extended" and move to samples/playbooks/extended. Decision: add a run-time badge in sample README. (DECIDED: Maya)
- Telemetry: standardize event verbs to present-tense and plural resource names (e.g., embeddings.create, completions.generate). Sofia to publish mapping table and a lint rule for samples repo. (ACTION: Sofia, due 2026-12-07)
- Rust quickstart: accept community contribution for initial port; internal sample will remain JS/Python for GA. (ACTION: Maya to ping contributors)
- Packaging: Jonah's pex prototype reduces friction for internal workshops; keep as experimental until Jan 2027. Conclude monorepo packaging decision in next architecture sync. (ACTION: Jonah)

Blockers (sticky items):
- RDW-1324: CI failures on samples site when node version 20.x used; currently blocking deploy previews. Impact: demo automation flaky. (OWNER: Ethan)
- RDW-1450: Telemetry schema mismatch between samples and Hosted API instrumentation pipeline. Causes noisy alerts in QA. (OWNER: Sofia)
- Missing Rust example content for playbook v0.3 (OWNER: Maya)

Action items (owner, clear next step, due date):
- Ethan: split samples CI into two pipelines (preview + build) to isolate node-version failures; aim to merge before next demo cycle. Due 2026-12-04.
- Sofia: publish telemetry mapping table to Confluence + add a simple eslint plugin to flag disallowed event names in samples. Due 2026-12-07.
- Jonah: finalize pex wheel prototype and write short how-to for R&D workshops; include size comparison. Due 2026-12-10.
- Maya: collect Rust quickstart volunteer(s) and add a tiny checklist for community contributions (license, test, demo gallery). Due 2026-12-06.
- Priya: add acceptance criteria to quickstart README template (runtime badge, cloud steps, known-limitations). Due 2026-12-03.

Risks / open questions:
- Demo stability for Dec customer review: if node CI keeps failing we may not be able to generate live preview links for the external demo. Contingency: use recorded runs + local hosted preview. (Plan: Ethan + Maya)
- Should quickstart playbook mandate a single bearer token pattern, or show both short-lived and long-lived token flows? (Action: Priya to propose in next doc pass)

Notes to self / rough ideas captured quickly:
- Consider a "playbook-lite" template for ML interns: 1) TL;DR, 2) 5-minute try, 3) troubleshooting checklist, 4) how to adapt to Dedicated/Private. Put in samples/playbooks/lite.
- Add a tiny script in samples repo that runs smoke tests against the Hosted API sandbox and returns a short report (pass/fail + token sanity). Could be used in CI preview. (Prototype: scripts/smoke-preview.sh)
- Try adding small web-based interactive snippets ("run-in-browser") for streaming output using WebSocket proxy; experiment in samples/interactive/websocket-play.

Links and quick refs (captured as artifacts too):
- GH PR: sdk change for esbuild (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482)
- GH PR: samples site refactor prototype (https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/197)
- Confluence: Quickstart Playbook Draft (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEVEX/Quickstart+Playbook+Draft)
- JIRA: RDW-1324 (samples CI failures)
- JIRA: RDW-1450 (telemetry schema mismatch)

Next meeting: 2026-12-07 10:15 PT — focus: playbook v0.3 approvals, CI isolation status, telemetry lint demo

End notes: quick, messy, still a draft — will tidy after Sofia publishes telemetry mapping and Ethan stabilizes node CI.

-- Maya (captured live)
